Part B conceptual MCQs
What is the direct substrate added to a growing DNA strand?
dNTP
dNMP; NTP; free base
A dNTP supplies the activated alpha phosphate; dNMP is the incorporated residue, NTP has ribose, and a free base lacks the backbone precursor.
Which group participates in the next polymerization reaction?
Primer 3′-OH
Template 5′ phosphate; primer 2′-OH; incoming base amino group
The primer hydroxyl attacks the alpha phosphate. The template guides identity but does not provide the growing hydroxyl.
Which direction describes ordinary polymerase proofreading?
3′→5′ exonuclease
5′→3′ polymerase; 5′→3′ exonuclease; internal endonuclease
Editing removes the newest nucleotide from the growing 3′ end; extension moves in the opposite direction.
Which activity of E. coli Pol I removes downstream RNA primer material?
5′→3′ nuclease
3′→5′ proofreading; helicase; ligase
Downstream 5′ end processing is distinct from editing the growing 3′ end; ligase seals rather than removes residues.
Why is G–C not selected at every template position?
Complementary geometry and catalytic alignment determine specificity
Three bonds always win; GTP is always more abundant; proofreading converts all pairs to G–C
The active site recognizes the template-dependent pair, not maximum hydrogen-bond number.
Which E. coli Pol III subunit carries its primary editing activity?
Epsilon (dnaQ)
Alpha (dnaE); beta clamp; DnaB
Alpha synthesizes DNA, beta is a processivity clamp and DnaB is a helicase.
Which eukaryotic nuclear replication polymerase lacks intrinsic proofreading?
Pol α
Pol δ; Pol ε; all three
Pol α initiates DNA synthesis after primase; δ and ε possess editing activity.
Which structure is the preferred direct substrate for ordinary polymerase proofreading?
A mismatched primer 3′ terminus
A fully paired fixed substitution; an internal double-strand break; intact methylated GATC
The exonuclease processes a growing end, not a distant internal substrate or a fixed complementary pair.
Which E. coli protein recognizes the mismatch?
MutS
MutH; Dam; DNA ligase
MutH incises the appropriate GATC site, Dam methylates it and ligase seals nicks.
Which property normally directs E. coli methyl-directed MMR toward the new strand?
Temporary lack of adenine methylation at GATC
CpG methylation; RNA cap; telomere length
The hemimethylated GATC site provides orientation; CpG and RNA capping are different processes.
Which enzyme creates the classical methyl-directed incision in E. coli?
MutH
MutS; UvrD; Pol III
MutH is an endonuclease; MutS recognizes, UvrD unwinds and Pol III can resynthesize.
Which factor unwinds DNA in the canonical E. coli MMR route?
UvrD
Dam; MutH; DNA ligase
UvrD helicase exposes the strand for excision; the other factors methylate, incise or seal.
What is the composition of human MutSα?
MSH2–MSH6
MSH2–MSH3; MLH1–PMS2; MLH1–MSH6
MSH2–MSH3 is MutSβ and MLH1–PMS2 is MutLα.
What is human MutLα?
MLH1–PMS2
MSH2–MSH6; MSH2–MSH3; RFC–PCNA
The MSH complexes recognize substrates; RFC loads PCNA, a clamp.
Which complex preferentially contributes to recognition of larger small insertion-deletion loops?
MutSβ
MutH; Pol α; ligase I
MSH2–MSH3 has loop-substrate preferences; recognition overlaps with MutSα.
What is PCNA?
A eukaryotic sliding clamp
A methyltransferase; an exonuclease; a dNTP
PCNA coordinates replication and repair proteins and can contribute to strand orientation.
What is the direct chemical product of proofreading hydrolysis of one terminal residue?
A nucleotide monophosphate
A dNTP; an amino acid; pyrophosphate alone
Hydrolysis cleaves the backbone; polymerization, not proofreading, releases pyrophosphate from a dNTP.
Which term describes the number of additions per productive enzyme association?
Processivity
Mutation frequency; fidelity; strand discrimination
Processivity concerns continuity of synthesis, while fidelity concerns sequence correctness.
What is a fixed substitution?
A changed complementary base pair that can be inherited
Every transient mismatch; any nick; every chemically modified base
A mismatch may be corrected; a nick alters continuity; a lesion is chemical damage.
Which mutation class is G–C to A–T?
Transition
Transversion; frameshift; inversion
G→A and C→T are within their respective base classes; both describe the same base-pair change.
Part C analytical and numerical problems
A polymerase makes 10⁻⁵ errors per addition; proofreading removes 99% and MMR removes 99.9% of survivors. What residual probability follows?
10⁻¹⁰
Multiply 10⁻⁵ × 0.01 × 0.001. The other choices represent uncorrected or partly corrected outcomes.
A 4 Mbp chromosome is duplicated completely. Error probability is 10⁻⁷ per newly added nucleotide. Expected errors across both daughter duplexes?
There are 8 million new nucleotide additions across both daughters, so 8×10⁶×10⁻⁷=0.8. The 0.4 choice counts one daughter.
For λ=0.2 independent rare residual events per daughter, approximate probability of at least one?
1−exp(−0.2)=0.18127. 0.8187 is the zero-event probability; the mean is not exactly the probability.
Correct and incorrect specificity constants are 10⁵ and 1 M⁻¹s⁻¹. Wrong nucleotide concentration is five times correct. Approximate wrong-to-correct flux ratio?
The ratio is (1×5)/(10⁵×1). Equal concentration would instead yield 10⁻⁵.
A mismatched end can extend at 4 s⁻¹ or be excised at 96 s⁻¹ in a two-exit model. What fraction escapes editing?
The first-event probability is 4/(4+96). 0.96 is the excision fraction, not escape.
Initial error 10⁻⁵, escape proofreading 10⁻², escape MMR 10⁻³. What is the double-deficient fold increase over wild type?
With neither correction layer the error is 10⁻⁵; divide by 10⁻¹⁰. The fold effects multiply under this model.
A methylated G-containing parental strand pairs incorrectly with T on its daughter strand. Which product should directed correction favor?
G–C
A–T; G–T; A–C
Removal of daughter T followed by copying G restores C. A–T would require inappropriate removal of G.
Reverse only methylation orientation in the same G–T heteroduplex. Which complementary product may become favored?
A–T
G–C necessarily; G–G; T–T
The orientation now favors using T as template, illustrating that strand identity is not inherent in base identity.
A purified E. coli MMR reaction binds mismatch normally but fails to nick hemimethylated GATC. Which specific defect is most directly supported?
MutH incision or its activation
Defective nucleotide selection; DNA ligase alone; a lack of primer hydroxyl
Recognition is intact; the blocked readout is incision. MutL signaling is also a possible cause, so MutH activity should be tested directly.
A defined E. coli reaction lacking MutH regains repair with a suitable pre-existing nick. What does that support?
The nick bypasses the usual incision requirement
MutH is the only repair protein; MutH is proofreading polymerase; repair no longer needs recognition
Supplying the intermediate can bypass its production, not the remainder of the pathway.
A mutant can extend correctly paired primer but cannot hydrolyze a mismatched 3′ end. Which defect is most directly demonstrated?
Proofreading exonuclease
MutS recognition; Dam methylation; ligase
The measured defect is terminal hydrolysis; internal mismatch repair requires a different substrate assay.
MSH2 loss disrupts both major nuclear MutS complexes. Loss of MSH6 primarily removes which?
MutSα
MutSβ; MutLα; both necessarily
MSH6 partners MSH2 in α; MSH3 is the distinct β partner.
A eukaryotic nick initially lies 3′ to a mismatch. How can 5′→3′ EXO1 still contribute?
MutLα-directed additional incision can provide a suitable 5′ entry
EXO1 must reverse its polarity in all cases; MutH methylates the site; ligase removes the mismatch
Additional incision resolves the geometric problem; alternative EXO1-independent pathways also exist.
An intact G–T heteroduplex persists to another replication round with no repair. What products arise from its two strands?
G–C and A–T
Two G–T; two G–C; two A–T
G templates C, and T templates A; one product is restored and the other is a complementary substitution.
An extra nucleotide loops out on the nascent strand in a repeat, then is retained and fixed. What change is expected?
Insertion
Deletion; inversion; translocation
The daughter strand contains an extra copied unit; a template loop can instead produce a deletion.
Forty of 100 independent cultures have no mutants. Under the zero-class model, what is m?
0.916 events per culture
−ln(0.40)=0.916. The zero fraction is not itself the mean event count.
If the preceding cultures each experienced 10⁶ divisions, estimated rate under the stated assumptions?
9.16×10⁻⁷ per division
0.916 per division; 4×10⁻⁵; 10⁶
Divide estimated events per culture by divisions per culture, not by number of cultures again.
An inhibitor reduces total synthesized molecules from 10,000 to 1,000 and erroneous molecules from 100 to 10. What happens to observed error fraction?
It remains 1%
It improves tenfold; worsens tenfold; becomes 0.1%
Both numerator and denominator decrease proportionally: 100/10000=10/1000.
Two error classes contribute 100 initial errors each. Proofreading leaves 1 A and 50 B; MMR leaves 10% of A and 20% of B. Expected survivors?
Class-specific expected counts are 0.1+10=10.1. Averaging unrelated escape fractions before weighting can mislead.
Two independent cultures contain 100 resistant cells each, one descended from one early mutation and another from many late events. What can be inferred from the counts alone?
The mutant counts do not establish equal mutation rates
Exactly 100 mutations occurred in each; rates must be zero; both must lack MMR
Clonal descendants are not independent mutation events; timing and growth matter.
Assertion–Reason (A: both true and reason explains assertion; B: both true but reason does not explain; C: assertion true, reason false; D: assertion false, reason true)
Assertion: MMR needs strand discrimination. Reason: an ordinary mismatch alone does not reveal which strand was originally correct.
A
B; C; D
Both are true; replacing the wrong strand can fix an altered pair, so orientation is needed.
Assertion: Pol α lacks intrinsic proofreading. Reason: all replicative polymerases contain the same exonuclease domain.
C
A; B; D
The assertion is correct; the reason is false because proofreading arrangements vary.
Assertion: Every bacterial MMR pathway uses MutH. Reason: E. coli has methyl-directed MutH-dependent incision.
D
A; B; C
The E. coli statement is true, but the mechanism is not universal.
Assertion: A fixed complementary mutation is not ordinarily recognized as a mismatch. Reason: correct Watson–Crick geometry can be retained after the sequence changes.
A
B; C; D
A complementary changed pair lacks the abnormal pairing geometry that mismatch recognition detects.
Assertion: PCNA is a sliding clamp. Reason: MSH2 is a shared subunit of MutSα and MutSβ.
B
A; C; D
Both statements are accurate but MSH2 composition does not explain the structure of PCNA.
Multiple statements and matching
Which statements hold? I: DNA synthesis is 5′→3′. II: proofreading can hydrolyze a 3′ terminal linkage. III: MutH is universal in bacteria. IV: MutS detects mismatches.
I, II and IV
I and III; II and III; all four
I, II and IV are correct; MutH is organism-specific.
Match E. coli factors to tasks: 1 MutS, 2 MutH, 3 UvrD, 4 ligase; a incision, b unwinding, c recognition, d sealing.
Recognition precedes incision, then helicase-supported processing and sealing.
Which statements hold? I: MSH2–MSH6 is MutSα. II: MSH2–MSH3 is MutSβ. III: human MLH1–PMS2 is MutLα. IV: MutLα is identical to E. coli MutH.
I, II and III
II and IV; I and IV; all four
The first three identify complexes correctly; MutLα is not identical to MutH.
Match term to description: 1 mismatch, 2 nick, 3 gap, 4 fixed substitution; a backbone interruption without missing residue, b absent residues, c abnormal pairing, d altered complementary pair.
These structures differ by pairing, continuity and sequence inheritance.

Which statements hold under the simple sequential error model? I: conditional escape probabilities multiply. II: E(X)=Np needs independence. III: P(X=0)=(1−p)ᴺ assumes independent equal-probability trials. IV: mutation frequency is always a mutation rate.
I and III
I and II; II and IV; all four
Expectation is additive even without independence; mutant frequency depends on clone growth and timing.
